justifications.functional_suitability: Web Application, API Gateway and Claims Core Domain Service cover submission (R-01) and adjuster handling (R-02). Claim Routing & Policy Engine with feature flags supports per-type migration (R-03). But no explicit claim intake or adjuster workflow components, and no migration cutover or rollback detail.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Read-Model & Caching Store (Redis, Cosmos DB projections, Query API Component) and asynchronous Integration & Sync Worker decouple screens from 5 s mainframe responses. Gaps: no latency budget, no autoscaling or capacity mechanisms, and the cache invalidation and projection lag are unspecified.
justifications.compatibility: Integrates with Corporate Active Directory via OIDC, with the mainframe via Enterprise Service Bus and Mainframe Adapter Component, and with the Audit & Compliance System. Gaps: batch window handling and the one-interface-change-per-quarter limit are unaddressed, and the ESB-to-mainframe protocol is vague. CDC feeds sync.
justifications.usability: React SPA Client and Node.js BFF serve customers, brokers and adjusters. Compliance officers and the Migration Support team reach only the same Web Application, with no dedicated audit views or ops console. The Replay API Controller is the sole support interface. No accessibility or UX mechanisms.
justifications.reliability: Sync Orchestrator Component with State & Deduplication Store (outbox, idempotency), Dead-Letter & Audit Handler and Replay API Controller address no loss or duplicates (R-04). Feature flags in Claim Routing & Policy Engine enable fallback. Gaps: no HA/DR, no explicit rollback procedure, and the nightly batch window is not handled.
justifications.security: Entra ID SSO via the BFF, JWT validation in Authentication Middleware, mTLS between services, Key Vault with HSM keys and managed identities, TDE, Row-Level Security, secret rotation, and audit export from Azure Monitor to the WORM Audit & Compliance System with temporal tables cover R-07 thoroughly.
justifications.maintainability: Clear container decomposition: BFF, API Gateway, Claims Core Domain Service with DDD domain model, Data Access Repository and Telemetry dispatcher, and a separate Integration & Sync Worker. Feature-flag routing supports per-type switch-back (R-06). Gaps: shared Azure SQL used for both domain and sync state, and no explicit rollback procedure.
justifications.portability: Hybrid on-prem and Azure is addressed via ExpressRoute/VPN and the ESB. However the design is tightly bound to Azure-specific services (Functions, Cosmos DB, Key Vault, Event Grid, Service Bus). No abstraction, containerization or IaC replaceability is specified, apart from the .NET Container Apps gateway.

sensitivity_points: Read-model freshness depends on projection lag
Cold-cache misses for partly mainframe data
tradeoffs: Fast reads versus eventual consistency of data
PERF-01.justification: Read models and Redis cache decouple screens from 5 s mainframe latency. But no explicit 2 s budget, no cache-miss or fallback path, and the Query API is not wired to the Web Application path. Plausible but unproven.

sensitivity_points: Azure SQL and Container Apps scaling configuration
tradeoffs: Async decoupling versus delayed mainframe confirmation
PERF-02.justification: Submissions land in Azure SQL and are forwarded asynchronously via Service Bus, which shields the mainframe. But autoscaling, throttling and batch-window scheduling of forwarding are not described, so protecting the batch window is unaddressed.

tradeoffs: Continuous availability versus delayed mainframe visibility
AVAIL-01.justification: Outbox pattern, Service Bus messaging, dead-lettering and a replay API let submissions persist in Azure SQL and be forwarded after the window. Explicit batch-window scheduling is not shown, but the mechanisms are largely present.

sensitivity_points: Idempotency key end-to-end including mainframe side
tradeoffs: Strong exactly-once semantics versus extra latency and complexity
AVAIL-02.justification: Outbox, idempotency tracking, dead-letter handling and manual replay support reconciliation without loss or duplicates. There is no automated reconciliation job against the mainframe, and mainframe-side deduplication is not stated, leaving a residual risk.

sensitivity_points: Data sync back to the mainframe on switch-back
tradeoffs: Flexible routing versus complexity of dual-write consistency
MOD-01.justification: Per-claim-type feature flags and routing support gradual migration and rollback. But the mainframe interface change is not addressed, and data reconciliation upon switch-back within one day is not described. Strangler pattern is implied but not explicit.

sensitivity_points: UI depends only on the gateway API contract
Data migration and cutover of the system of record
tradeoffs: Stable UI contract versus gateway abstraction effort
MOD-02.justification: UIs talk only to the BFF and gateway, with domain logic behind them, so switching the system of record does not touch the UIs. The Azure SQL database is already the modern store. The final data cutover plan is not detailed.

sensitivity_points: Broker identity must map to RLS predicate
tradeoffs: Database-level enforcement versus cross-system policy consistency
SEC-01.justification: RLS and JWT validation help in the new platform, and audit events flow to the audit system. However, broker-to-customer ownership rules are not described, and nothing enforces authorization in the mainframe. Denial recording is only implied.

sensitivity_points: Mainframe credentials not tied to AD
tradeoffs: Short tokens improve revocation but add refresh load
SEC-02.justification: OIDC SSO with JWT validation against AD revokes access on the new platform if tokens are short-lived, but token lifetime and session handling are unspecified. Mainframe user access is not linked to AD, so revocation in both systems is unaddressed.
